correctness.rationale: Opposite fixed endpoints decouple the two arcs. Updating the interior sites from one endpoint in sequence to copy its opinion is a positive-rate path to the one-interface set, by sweeping away all other walls. A one-interface state remains in that set and the resulting reflecting walk is irreducible (with a singleton state on the one-edge arc). The arc count ratios are q and 1/q, so the stationary variance is the sum of the two truncated-geometric variances and is invariant under q to 1/q. Logarithmic differentiation twice gives W_L; at q=1 the uniform laws give (V_1,V_2,V_3)=(2,3/2,4/3), proving strictness at that endpoint. For q<1 the two exact differences have signs opposite P and Q at z=q+1/q. Each z-2 shifted polynomial has one Descartes sign change and a negative constant, establishing existence and uniqueness of a root above 2; opposite signs at z=27/10 strictly separate the roots. The map back to q reverses their ordering, and the sign comparisons give all three minimizing placements and the two exact ties. A separate exact symbolic and 16-state-generator replay, /workspace/branches/649dd4b5-5b89-417a-8842-335f1ed67568/replay_record3.py, with output in replay_record3_results.txt in the same directory, reproduced the factorizations, roots and all three q=4/9 fractions and verified V_2<V_3<V_1. Here the strict intermediate optimum is the discrete placement a=2 at fixed q, not an optimum over q. The uploaded checker was inspected but not executed. The general-in-q proof is analytic and does not rest on the finite generator comparisons.

value.rationale: Stationary total-count fluctuations are a natural objective not captured by expected support or extreme-event probabilities. The first cycle with a genuinely intermediate spacing shows that neither endpoint placement is always best, on a nonempty open interval with exact boundaries and ties. This is a meaningful minimal model and a complete classification within it, not evidence of a larger-cycle phase law.
